subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Finlytics
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@finlytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks for taking the time today — great overview of Redwood's Dedicated offering. I wanted to capture a few things from our side while they're fresh and confirm next steps.

Quick context: Finlytics is an analytics platform processing nightly batch jobs and real-time scoring for ~25M events/day. We're currently self-hosting models (PyTorch) on a k8s cluster with autoscaling; the big pain points are:
- 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during peak scoring windows (often EOD) causing downstream SLA misses
- Multi-tenant noise — we need stronger isolation for regulatory reasons and to guarantee performance for a couple of key customers
- Cold-starts and unpredictable throughput when we scale up for short bursts

Success criteria for evaluating Dedicated: predictable TPS at 95th percentile, <250ms token latency for customer-facing scoring, and clear isolation/PII controls (KMS + audit logs). Procurement also needs an initial cost estimate and an SOW we can review.

I can loop in Tom (ops/infra) for the technical deep-dive — he's CCed. Next steps on our side:
1) Internal review of capacity estimate/SOW
2) Procurement timing: likely aiming for PO in ~6 weeks if numbers look good

Thanks again — looking forward to the materials you mentioned.

Best,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Platform
Finlytics

--
Sofia Ramirez
Finlytics | sofia@finlytics.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@finlytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and for looping Tom in. Below is a recap from our call plus proposed next steps so everyone has a single source of truth.

Recap (pain points & current stack)
- Latency spikes at 95/99p during EOD scoring windows; current k8s autoscaling leads to slow cold-starts.
- Need for workload isolation: regulatory customers require stricter separation than your current multi-tenant configs provide.
- Bursty traffic profile: baseline ~200 TPS for scoring with spikes up to ~400 TPS for 10-20 minute windows during nightly jobs and campaign bursts.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 controls, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs are must-haves.

What Redwood Dedicated can provide (fit summary)
- Reserved GPU pools (dedicated capacity) to guarantee throughput; we can size pools to hit your baseline 200 TPS and support short burst capacity to ~400 TPS (burst policy) while preserving isolation.
- Predictable performance: we use pinned capacity + smart routing to reduce noisy neighbor effects and keep 95p latency stable.
- Autoscale + burst model: configurable burst headroom (we typically recommend short-duration burst credits for traffic patterns like yours).
- Compliance: Private deployment options, KMS integrations, and extended audit logs are available; we'll provide SOC 2 evidence and architecture notes.

Initial sizing & assumptions (attached):
- Baseline target: 200 TPS sustained
- Burst target: up to 400 TPS for up to 15 minutes, on-demand
- Working assumption: model architecture similar to what you described (seq2seq scoring, moderate context lengths).
- Attachment: capacity_estimate.xlsx (high-level sizing + cost envelope) and RD_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (draft SOW with milestones).

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (score/infra) — Vanessa to run an on-call session with Tom to validate model footprints and exact GPU SKU mapping.
2) Procurement review — Aditya will share a pricing/term outline and a suggested pilot commitment to reduce procurement friction.
3) Legal/SOW iteration — We'll turn the attached draft into a version that includes your timeline and any compliance riders.

Requested sequencing: can Vanessa + Tom connect for a 60-min technical session next week? We have availability Tue/Wed morning PST.

I'll also link the HubSpot opportunity and upload the walkthrough notes to the shared Drive for your team.

Thanks — will follow up with calendar invites once we confirm availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: capacity_estimate.xlsx, RD_SOW_draft_v1.pdf
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — pricing & pilot suggestion

Sofia — quick note on commercial approach so Finlytics has something to react to during procurement.

Recommended pilot: 6-month pilot with reserved capacity sized to baseline (200 TPS) and an agreed burst policy (up to 400 TPS for 15 minutes, capped at X burst credits per day). Pilot commits help lock a predictable unit cost and let us validate latency SLA in your environment.

Estimated resources (back-of-envelope): 2-4x A100-class GPUs (depending on model footprint & batching) in a dedicated pool to meet the baseline and burst headroom. Final SKU/count will be confirmed after Vanessa's workload profiling.

Commercial asks:
- PO timeline target: 6 weeks from now (per Sofia's note)
- Redlines: we'll accept typical procurement requests but will need to scope any compliance add-ons (e.g., HSM) separately.

I'll share a first-pass term sheet and a HubSpot opportunity link for tracking. Marissa — can you confirm the preferred pilot sizing (2 vs 4 GPUs) after the tech deep-dive?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
